title: Scope, intake and the boundary with carpet and upholstery
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: LeadSmart NSW: renovating and maintenance (no date in page body; page metadata shows published 2026-05-18 and modified 2026-07-20); WorkSafe Queensland, Asbestos removal and licensing (no date shown); SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences (no date shown).
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Furniture restorers who take in timber and upholstered pieces, and staff who answer enquiries and set up jobs.
learningOutcomes: Describe the scope of furniture restoration and separate it from in-place carpet and upholstery cleaning.
Ask the intake questions that decide whether a piece is in scope.
Record a scope decision, with its reason, before any work or quote is issued.

instruction.heading: What furniture restoration covers
instruction.body: In this course, restoration means working on a furniture piece in a workshop or at the business's premises. It includes stripping and refinishing timber, repairing joints and veneer, and renewing the fabric, foam and backing of an upholstered piece. It does not mean cleaning fabric in place in a client's home or office. That work is taught in the carpet and upholstery cleaning course, including the fibre identification lesson “Fibre and construction identification” (Fibre and construction identification). The two courses are kept apart so that a cleaner does not take on a restoration job without the checks taught here.

instruction.heading: Intake questions
instruction.body: Ask what the piece is, where it came from, and its age if known. Ask what finish or fabric the client believes it has, whether it has been stripped, repaired or re-covered before, and whether it has been kept in a damp, smoky, flooded or contaminated place. Ask whether children or pets use it, and what result the client wants. Record the answers. They decide whether the job is in scope and which checks come first. If the piece has been affected by mould, fire, smoke, flood or biohazard contamination, stop intake and refer the job to the High-risk cleaning module. Do not start restoration on it.

instruction.heading: Deciding in, conditional or out
instruction.body: A job is in scope, conditional, or refused. A conditional job goes ahead only after a named check is passed, such as the screening in “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer”. A refused job is one the business cannot do safely or lawfully with the people, equipment or licences it holds. Refuse work that needs a licence the business does not hold, and say so in writing. Record every decision and its reason before work starts or a quote is sent, using the business's approved procedure {{business:procedures.approved_sop}}.

procedure: Record the client's details and a description of the item, with photos.
Ask the intake questions and record the answers.
Check the answers for out-of-scope triggers, including contamination and any licensed work.
Decide whether the job is in scope, conditional or refused, and record the reason.
Tell the client in writing what happens next and what is needed before work starts.

workedExamples.situation: A client brings a timber dining chair from a rental flat where the roof leaked. The client wants a quick strip and polish before a dinner on Sunday. The seat has been re-stuffed and the client does not know what is under the fabric.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the job in scope, and what happens next?
workedExamples.reasoning: The job is conditional at best. Water damage raises a mould question, and mould is in the High-risk cleaning module, not this course. The stuffed seat has an unknown backing that needs screening before any cutting or stripping. Record the intake, do not start work, tell the client the timing depends on the mould check and screening, and do not promise the Sunday date.

equipmentAndPpe: Intake form or job card, from the business's approved set
Camera or tablet for item photos
Business PPE as set out in the approved list {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Accepting a job before knowing the finish or the backing.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete intake and screening first, and record the answers.

commonErrors.error: Treating upholstery cleaning in a client's home and furniture restoration in the workshop as the same job.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the job against the scope boundary, and refer cleaning in place to the carpet and upholstery course.

commonErrors.error: Declining a job without recording why.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the scope decision and reason on the job record, and tell the client in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Older furniture finishes and backings can carry lead and asbestos hazards. NSW's house guidance links lead-based paint to homes built before 1970 (page metadata modified 20 July 2026); the guidance is written for houses, not furniture. Intake questions are the first screening step only. They do not replace testing or a specialist assessment (see “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer”).

This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate or authority to do regulated work. Work that needs a licence, such as asbestos removal, must be held by the business and by the people doing the work, as the state or territory regulator requires. Queensland requires a Class A licence even for small amounts of friable asbestos, and a Class B licence once non-friable asbestos exceeds ten square metres (no page date shown). South Australia puts friable and non-friable removal under Class A with no area cap, and reserves Class B for non-friable material above ten square metres (no page date shown). The business's recorded licence position is {{business:compliance.licence_requirements}}.
Check the regulator for the state or territory where the job is done.

qualityStandard: Every job has a written scope decision before work starts or a quote is issued.
Every refused or conditional job has a recorded reason.
The client has written confirmation of the next step.
documentationEvidence: Intake record with client details, item description, photos and intake answers
Scope decision (in, conditional or refused) and the reason
Written confirmation sent to the client
summary: Furniture restoration is workshop work on a piece. Cleaning fabric in place is the carpet and upholstery course.
Intake answers decide scope. Contamination and licensed work stop or refer the job.
Every decision is recorded with its reason before work or a quote starts.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client brings a timber chair that was stored in a damp garage and has black marks on it. What is the first step?
options: Start stripping, because the marks are probably surface stains that will come off easily with a light sanding and a clean
Stop intake, check for mould before any work or quote, and refer under the High-risk module if mould is present
Quote a fixed price and clean the marks on site, since the client wants a quick answer on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Which work belongs to the carpet and upholstery cleaning course rather than this course?
options: Re-foaming a restored armchair in the workshop
Stripping a timber table in the workshop
Cleaning the fabric in place on a client's sofa at home

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the business record the reason for declining a restoration job?
options: It shows the scope decision was made on the facts and supports the business's records
It is not needed if the client agrees to the decision on the day and signs the form
It replaces the written quote that the client has already signed for the job at the start
